data.name: Smita
data.gender_notes: Smita is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root smi, 'to smile' — smita, 'a smile'. Its root is Sanskrit smi (स्मि). A classical Sanskrit term for a smile. Smita is a Sanskrit name meaning “Smiling; a smile”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Smita expresses “Smiling; a smile”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root smi, 'to smile' — smita, 'a smile'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Smita total 17, reducing to 8. Number 8 is associated with ambition, authority and material mastery.

vedic_reference.note: Smita is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'shamana' (soothing, calming) and 'abhimana' (desire, passion). It is a popular name among the Hindi speaking population and is also used in other Indian languages such as Tamil and Telugu. In Hindu mythology, Smita is associated with the goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and wisdom.
